thread.title: Apple Stock Could Rise Because Weak iPhone Sales Are 'Baked In'

title: Apple Stock Could Rise Because Weak iPhone Sales Are 'Baked In'
text:
Apple Stock Could Rise Because Weak iPhone Sales Are Already ‘Baked In’ By Dec. 13, 2018 11:37 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Daniel Acker/Bloomberg Text size
Weaker demand for the latest iPhones is now priced into Apple ’s stock, according to Piper Jaffray.
The firm’s analyst Michael Olson lowered his price target for Apple stock (ticker: AAPL) to $222 from $250, but he reiterated his Overweight rating for the shares. He cited positive results from its annual survey of U.S. iPhone users.
“Given the solid U.S. demand observed in our survey, weaker iPhone-component-supplier results must be due to slower int’l uptake,” he wrote on Thursday. “Regarding Apple shares, we believe international iPhone weakness and disappointment around lack of future unit disclosure are both largely baked into the stock.”
Apple stock was up 1.7%, to $171.89, on Thursday. Olson’s reduced price target implies upside of more than 29%.
Listen to a conversation between Avi Salzman and Alex Eule about the revolution of subscriptions—and whether a subscription model could work for Apple—in this recent episode of The Readback. You can sign up for the podcast in iTunes or wherever you listen to podcasts .
The company’s shares have declined more than 20% since the end of October as concerns have mounted about weak demand for the newest iPhone models, amid guidance warnings from several component suppliers.
Last month, The Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Apple cut orders for all three newly released iPhone models.
But Olson said Piper Jaffray’s survey of more than 550 U.S. iPhone users revealed that upgrade rates for the latest iPhone models was slightly better than 2017’s survey levels.
Olson also noted that Apple’s current valuation of 12 times forward earnings was below its two-year average of 15 times.
“We believe a price target multiple that is a slight premium to the two-year historical average is reasonable due to a large and entrenched base of active Apple device users,” he wrote.
